_comment: Does the phantom third potion slot (RunEngine.cs:727 advertises it, RunRewardGenerator.cs:1015
cannot fill it) show up as fewer potions at the boss? Measured evaluation-only over 3,500 act1
promotion seeds on the checkpoint every census figure uses, in seven 500-seed shards.
Answer: no -- and the honest answer is that this comparison cannot address the question, because
exposure is defined by already holding two potions. See 'confound'.
Two independent validations of the instrumentation: it reproduces the committed terminal census
25 cleared), and no arrival ever holds a potion in the third slot

arrival_rate_by_exposure.note: a selection marker, not an effect: reaching a shop while already holding two potions requires a run that survived that far and met more shops on the way

confound: exposure is conditioned on the outcome variable. A potion-capacity refusal can only occur while the first two slots are already full, so 'refused before the boss' selects for runs carrying two potions -- which is why that group arrives with MORE usable potions (act 1: 1.595 vs 1.239; act 2: 1.378 vs 1.071), not fewer.

the same selection explains the arrival-rate gap (10.6% of exposed episodes reach a boss vs 3.1% of unexposed) and the higher shop count in the exposed group (1.811 vs 0.935 in act 1, 1.676 vs 1.0 in act 2). Richer runs meet more shops and more bosses.

so this study is uninformative about the cost of the phantom slot by construction, and no re-analysis of these rows repairs it. An unconfounded version holds the potion state fixed and varies what is offered -- episodes at two potions where a third was offered and refused against episodes at two potions where nothing was offered -- or compares the refused potion against what executed instead.
established: the phantom third slot is empty everywhere it can be seen: 0 of 162 boss arrivals hold a potion in slot 3, while 77 arrive at the engine's real capacity of two -- consistent with AddPotion scanning only min(2, len) slots (RunRewardGenerator.cs:1015)

the instrumentation agrees with the committed terminal census by an independent path: 162 arrivals split {'act1_overgrowth': 83, 'act2_underdocks': 79}, 25 cleared, and every cleared arrival is act-2 generated -- the same 83/79 arrival and 25/0 conversion split

a terminal RunPhase.Complete is not a clear: 161 of 162 arrivals end in that phase, because RunEngine.cs:1286-1293 sets it on a loss as well. Only the compound test (Complete AND State.LastPlayerWon) reproduces the census's 25 wins, which is the field-level mechanism behind the known trap that floor 17 cannot tell dying at the boss from beating it
potion purchases are rare in absolute terms: 0.533 per episode across 3,500 episodes, and 700 episodes (20.0%) meet a refusal before any boss
not_established: any causal statement about the phantom slot -- see 'confound'
whether removing the phantom slot would change win rate or depth; that needs a counterfactual the 2026-09-02 PPO freeze bars, or an engine change the operator owns
what the exposed episodes gave up: the refused action and the executed substitute are both recoverable from the probe rows, but no value comparison was computed
scope: simulator_act1 label, mixed-act population, argmax, one checkpoint, 3,500 seeds
